title: streaming SSE chunking/backpressure debug notes
body:
Context:
- Observed intermittent stalls in streaming text responses (SSE / text/event-stream) from hosted API routes. Client sometimes gets first N tokens then stream pauses for 5-30s, then finishes with a large chunk or completes immediately. Intermittent, not 100% reproducible but higher frequency on certain routes (longer generation, models with larger kv cache).

Services / route info:
- service: inference-proxy (node/express -> python/gunicorn -> model worker pool)
- route: POST /v1/streaming/generate
- model variant: redwood-compat/gpt-7b-quant (recent deploy 2025-02-10, commit: a3f2b7e)

What we've tried / repro commands (client side):
1) curl (raw, no buffering):
   curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
     -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streaming/generate \
     -d '{"prompt":"long prompt...","max_tokens":512}'
   - Observed behavior: initially streams a few events (small data chunks), then no activity for ~10s, then a burst of many events. --no-buffer / -N didn't prevent stalls.

2) node fetch (ReadableStream reader):
   const res = await fetch(url, opts);
   const reader = res.body.getReader();
   while (true) {
     const { value, done } = await reader.read();
     if (done) break;
     process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
   }
   - Observed: reader.read() sometimes blocks; backend logs show generation continued (tokens produced) but bytes didn't arrive at client until flush/batch boundary.

3) python aiohttp streaming client:
   async with session.post(url, json=payload) as r:
       async for chunk in r.content.iter_chunked(1024):
           print(chunk)
   - same intermittent stalls, chunk sizes vary widely.

Server-side attempts / changes tried:
- Added explicit res.flushHeaders() in express proxy after headers and after each SSE event. No clear change in frequency.
- Forced smaller chunk writes from model worker (flushed every token) to see if problem is worker batching. Slightly reduced stall length but still present.
- Disabled nginx buffering (proxy_buffering off) on a test host. That reduced stalls for some clients, but not all.

Logs / snippets (anonymized):
- worker logs (token generation timestamps):
  [2025-02-27 14:03:12.214] token=1
  [2025-02-27 14:03:12.318] token=2
  [2025-02-27 14:03:12.421] token=3
  ...
  [2025-02-27 14:03:25.512] token=45
- proxy access log (bytes sent / timestamps):
  2025-02-27T14:03:12.220Z GET /v1/streaming/generate 200 120 bytes
  2025-02-27T14:03:12.330Z GET /v1/streaming/generate 200 68 bytes
  2025-02-27T14:03:25.520Z GET /v1/streaming/generate 200 4096 bytes
  -> shows generation continuing but bytes from proxy arrive in big chunk at 14:03:25, indicating buffering somewhere.

Hypotheses:
1) Upstream buffering at one of the proxies (nginx / envoy) is accumulating small writes and flushing on heuristic (time/size) or by internal buffering. Evidence: turning off proxy_buffering helped on one host.
2) Node/Gunicorn wsgi buffering: gunicorn or the python server/framework buffers chunks until certain thresholds.
3) TCP Nagle or small-packet coalescing on host network path: but curl --no-buffer should mitigate; also burst sizes inconsistent.
4) Backpressure at client: some client-side event loops only read periodically. But observed across diverse clients.
5) Chunked encoding vs SSE framing mismatch: if server writes SSE events but doesn't write the trailing double-newline properly, some clients may wait for delimiter. Need to confirm event boundaries and ensure CRLF rules.
6) SSL termination (load balancer) buffering or TCP proxying causing delays when many tiny writes.

Commands / tests to run (next):
- Repro matrix (automated): run 100 sequential curl -N requests with a fixed prompt and log time-to-first-byte, total time, bytes per second. Compare with and without nginx buffering and with keepalive settings.
- Toggle gzip compression off/on (some proxies buffer to compute compression).
- Run a synthetic server that writes a token every 50ms directly behind LB to test if infrastructure is culprit:
  node synthetic-sse.js:
    res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', Connection: 'keep-alive' });
    let i=0; setInterval(()=>{ res.write(`data: token ${i}\n\n`); i++; }, 50);
  curl -N to synthetic endpoint and observe. If synthetic still stalls, infra issue.

- Use tcpdump / Wireshark on host to inspect packet timing to see if packets are sent immediately or buffered.
- Instrument proxy to log flush events (if possible) or enable debug for envoy/nginx upstream flush.

Repro commands to save (quick):
- curl stream (baseline):
  curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/streaming/generate \
    -d '{"prompt":"<RANDOM_PROMPT>","max_tokens":256}' 2>&1 | tee curl-stream.log

- node client (minimal):
  node -e "(async()=>{const r=await fetch(process.env.URL,{method:'POST',body:JSON.stringify({prompt:'a',max_tokens:256}),headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json','Authorization':'Bearer '+process.env.KEY}}); const rd=r.body.getReader(); for(;;){const{value,done}=await rd.read(); if(done)break; process.stdout.write(new TextDecoder().decode(value))}})()"  > node-stream.log

- synthetic server (local test):
  cat > synthetic-sse.js <<'EOF'
  const http=require('http');
  http.createServer((req,res)=>{
    res.writeHead(200,{ 'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache','Connection':'keep-alive' });
    let i=0;
    const t=setInterval(()=>{ res.write(`data: ${i}\n\n`); i++; if(i>200) { clearInterval(t); res.end(); } }, 50);
  }).listen(8081,()=>console.log('listening'))
  EOF
  curl -N http://localhost:8081/ | ts > synthetic.log

Observations to record during tests:
- ttfb (time to first byte), inter-chunk latency distribution (mean, p50, p95), chunk sizes, number of chunks per second.
- correlate with worker token production timestamps to see if network/proxy stalls introduced.

Quick notes / heuristics:
- If disabling compression fixes it, proxy is buffering to compress blocks.
- If synthetic server (no model, local) still stalls behind same LB, then infra; if not, worker batching or framework buffering likely.
- For SSE remember double-newline delimiter; some clients expect CRLF (
) vs LF only — try writing CRLF explicitly.

Immediate TODOs (owner: Samir):
- [ ] Create automated curl test harness and run 1000 trials across two regions (us-west/us-east) and with different LBs (nginx vs envoy).
- [ ] Run synthetic-sse behind our infra and behind raw host (bypass LB) to isolate layer.
- [ ] Add detailed logging to proxy for flush events and response write calls (timestamps).
- [ ] Try turning off gzip and proxy buffering in staging.
- [ ] Coordinate with infra / networking (Noah) to capture tcpdump on a failing request.

Notes / random thoughts:
- We recently changed gunicorn worker class from gevent->uvicorn (async) around commit a3f2b7e; check if intermediate framework behavior changed flush semantics.
- Some clients (python requests) will buffer until chunk size > 512 bytes; we should document recommended client patterns and examples in SDKs.

If anyone picks this up: start with synthetic-sse behind LB and confirm whether problem reproduces. Attach logs from both worker token timestamps and proxy access/flush times.

-- Samir
